note: The keeper's own pages (docs/future/13 section 2.4), written in the walker's hand and kept in the journal: the first opens by itself at the spring on the first evening. Each is { id, form, title, body: [lines] } in the letters' light markup (src/ui/journal-letters.js); an empty line starts a new paragraph. Under 60 words each. The first page's text is a stand-in until the story collaborator's arrives. The second (tend) shows as a centered card when you wake from your first rest (or at the first dawn, for a player who never rested), one click closes it, and it is kept here after the first (Phase 1 fix F15; stand-in text, words approved October 25, 2026, until the story collaborator's arrive). Set pieces add their pages here (docs/future/14; src/world/setpieces/live.js sets keeper:<id> when one is due): the cairns and the old keeper's letter under the last cairn, the passing boat, and the old fisherman's letters from it (form From the boat, the last asking for a dock, had as each gift is taken up; their order in recipes/setpieces/boat.json). A body line may be { if, line } or { not, line }: shown only when the journal holds (or lacks) that flag, so a page follows what you did.

words.entryLine: In your own hand, from the morning you came.
words.entryLineMany: In your own hand, since the morning you came.
words.title: Keeper's pages

pages.title: The first page
body: I came in on the morning tide. The land here is new, still pale from the sea.
Keepers don't own the islands we tend. We help them hold what comes, and write down what we see.
Someone will read this after me. Start at the spring.

pages.title: What a keeper does
body: A keeper doesn't build. A keeper tends.
Shape the land and let the tide shape it back. Make room for water, plants and shelter, and the creatures will find it, each in its own time.
The island grows while you are away: ebb, and flow, and ebb again.

pages.title: The cairns
body: They came one at a time, at dawn, all that spring. Flat stones, stacked by someone careful. I never saw who.

body.line: I added a stone to one, and the next morning's cairn had one more. Someone was answering.
I left them as I found them. Each leaned toward the next, and I followed.

body: At the end, a letter. I have left them standing.

pages.title: Under the last stone
body: If you are reading this, you followed them all the way. Good. Most never look up from the ground long enough.
I kept this island before you. It kept me, really.
Leave the cairns standing. Someone likes to know the way is still marked.

pages.title: The lantern on the water
body: A fishing boat lay off the island at dusk, a lantern in its wheelhouse, a bell when the swell moved it. It never came closer.

body.line: I left a parcel on the flat stone by the mooring. By morning the boat was gone, and something lay there in its place.
I watched until the lamp went out. By morning it was gone.

body: Whoever they are, they know this shore has a keeper now.

pages.title: A note, in pencil
body: Thank you for the parcel. I don't put in near islands much. Yours had a light on the shore, the only one for miles.
Seeds, for whatever ground you have.

pages.title: A second note
body: Your herbs kept the whole trip. I made tea of them in the wheelhouse on the long nights.
More seeds. These like a sunny bank.

pages.title: A note, folded small
body: Weather off the point last week. I thought of you out there with your one fire.
Here is some cord, the good kind. It holds wet or dry.

pages.title: A longer note
body: I keep your notes in a tin by the wheel now.
When the wind is right I can see your fire from the channel. A strange comfort, a fire with no town around it.

pages.title: A note, in a careful hand
body: Forty years on this water, and I still like a letter better than a catch.
These seeds are from a cliff where I put in. They might like your shore.

pages.title: A note, with a pressed flower
body: I count the visits by your stone now, not the tides.
The nets are hard on these hands lately. Cord for you, from the last good coil.

pages.title: A note, the paper soft
body: You never ask anything of me, so I've stopped asking what to send. I send what I'd want, if I kept an island.
The boat is old, like me. She deserves a quiet harbour one day.

pages.title: A note, tied with cord
body: I'll ask you something, the once.
Your shore has no place for a boat my size. If you built a dock out past the mooring, I could bring her in instead of lying off in the swell.
No hurry. I'll keep coming either way.

pages.title: A short note
body: All well aboard. Your light is still the first I look for.

pages.title: A short note
body: Fair weather this time. Thank you, as ever.

pages.title: A short note
body: The tin by the wheel is nearly full. I'll need a second.
